cur:objects2-castledermot-north-cross.summary: The Crucifixion fills the centre of the head on the east face of the North Cross at Castledermot, surrounded by the twelve apostles in rows on the arms and shaft. Lower down, a raven brings bread to the desert hermits Paul and Anthony, a monastic image of the Eucharist, above a spiral-carved base.
facts: The other face of the same cross carries a musician playing a lyre (cruit), one of the best-known images of an early Irish instrument.
cur:objects2-castledermot-north-cross.notes: Scene identifications from the photographer's detailed Commons description (A. F. Borchert).

wga:zgothic/mosaics/0prassed/2apse1.summary: High in the apse, Christ in golden robes stands on clouds tinged with red against a deep blue sky, raising his right hand, while the hand of God above holds out a wreath. Saints Peter and Paul present Praxedes and Pudentiana to him, and at the far left Pope Paschal I, with the square halo of the living, offers a model of the church; palm trees frame the scene, one crowned by a small haloed bird, and lambs process below. On the arch above, the Lamb on his throne appears among angels, completing a vision of heavenly glory.
facts: Pope Paschal I (817–824) rebuilt the church and commissioned its mosaics as part of his campaign of bringing martyrs' relics from the catacombs into the city.
Paschal's monogram appears at the top of the apse, and a dedicatory inscription in Latin runs beneath the lambs.

On the arch above, the symbols of the four Evangelists surround the Lamb on a throne, which Wikipedia describes as a symbol of Christ's return; the church also contains Paschal's celebrated mosaic chapel of Saint Zeno, built for his mother Theodora.
wga:zgothic/mosaics/0prassed/2apse1.notes: The WGA titles the work 'Christ's Second Coming' and dates it 822; the apse is usually dated to Paschal's pontificate (817–824). Medium on WGA ('Photo') was wrong. Figure identifications at the right of the image (e.g. St Zeno) were not confirmed.
